Farheen Zaman

Petroleum & Mining Engineer | Computational Modeling and Machine Learning for Energy Systems

Dhaka, Bangladesh

I am a petroleum and mining engineer (BSc, Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, CGPA 3.52/4.00, ranked 9th in class) who works at the intersection of numerical simulation and machine learning. My research covers finite element modeling of thermal-fluid systems in COMSOL, including nanofluid cooling, feedback flow control and bioconvection, and data-driven models for subsurface and energy problems, including well-log petrophysics and CO₂ adsorption.

I have co-authored four manuscripts (one published, three under review) and presented at an international conference. Alongside research, I have worked in plant operations and manufacturing supply, which keeps my modeling grounded in how real equipment behaves. I am preparing to pursue doctoral research on flow, transport and energy systems, where physics-based simulation and machine learning work together.

Research

My work combines physics-based simulation with data-driven modeling. Each project links a physical system to a numerical or machine learning method.

Boosting and Hybrid Machine Learning for Clay Weight Percentage Estimation from XRD and Well Logs: North Cook Inlet Field, Alaska

Published, Applied Computing and Geosciences (2026) · Co-author

Clay content controls how a rock stores and releases oil and gas, but lab measurement (XRD) is costly and covers few depths. We trained boosting models and stacked hybrids to estimate clay percentage from routine well logs, using 192 core samples from the Kitchen Lights Unit 1 well.

  • Best hybrid model reached a test R² of about 0.97 on a random split.
  • SHAP analysis identified thermal neutron porosity as the most influential log.
  • Depth-blocked validation and a transfer test in the Montney Formation probed generalization.

Dynamic Thermal Control of Nanofluid Systems: P, PI and PID Controllers in Hybrid Cooling Circuits

Under review · First author

Electronics and compact heat exchangers need cooling that reacts to changing heat loads. We simulated an Al₂O₃-water nanofluid cooling a square cavity with four heated cylinders, using P, PI and PID controllers to adjust inlet flow so a probe at the center holds 300 K.

  • Finite element model in COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2, validated against a published benchmark.
  • P control leaves a steady-state error; PI removes it; PID damps overshoot best.
  • A constant cooling circuit alongside the controlled one prevents uncontrolled temperature rise.

Thermo-Bioconvection of Oxytactic Microorganisms in a Lid-Driven Square Enclosure with a Rotating Porous Cylinder

Under review, International Communications in Heat and Mass Transfer · Co-author

Swimming microorganisms that seek oxygen can stir a fluid and change how heat and mass move through it. We modeled an enclosure with a moving lid and a rotating porous cylinder, and studied how flow, heat transfer (Nusselt number) and mass transfer (Sherwood number) respond to the governing dimensionless parameters.

  • Finite element model of flow, heat, oxygen and microorganism density with a Brinkman-Forchheimer-Darcy porous domain.
  • Heat transfer rises with Reynolds, Grashof and solutal Rayleigh numbers, and falls with cylinder rotation, Péclet and Lewis numbers.

Shallow to Deep Learning Models for Predicting CO₂ Adsorption on KOH-Activated Biochar

Under review, Journal of Porous Materials · Co-author

Biochar activated with KOH is a low-cost material for capturing CO₂. We compared five machine learning models and ten neural network architectures for predicting CO₂ uptake under different conditions.

  • Tree-based models reached R² up to 0.986; neural networks reached 0.97 to 0.99.
  • SHAP and partial dependence plots showed pressure and temperature dominate, and confirmed the boost from KOH activation.

Automatic Classification of Well Test Plots of Shale Gas Reservoirs Using a Convolutional Neural Network

Undergraduate thesis · Lead author

Interpreting well test pressure plots by hand is slow and subjective. This proof-of-concept trains a convolutional neural network to recognize four categories of well test plots from images.

  • Custom three-block CNN trained with image augmentation on a small curated dataset of about 200 plots.
  • About 89% validation accuracy, showing image-based classification of well test plots is feasible.

Finned Double-Pipe Heat Exchanger for Engine Oil Cooling

Heat Transfer Lab · Supervisor: Md. Mahamudul Hashan, SUST

A double-pipe heat exchanger designed to cool engine oil with water in a counter-flow arrangement, using copper fins to maximize heat transfer and thermal efficiency. The project covered the full workflow: a SolidWorks model of the geometry, an ANSYS CFD analysis of the temperature field, and physical fabrication of the unit.
